acceptance_condition: Returns (a) at least four findings from the Shapiro file, each a quote or close paraphrase carrying the file-relative citation and the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), and (b) at least three design constraints for persistence/concurrency (including at least one explicit split between CRDT-enforced and runtime-enforced invariants), each labeled as design inference.
rationale: Shapiro et al. 2011 is the corpus's only distributed-systems treatment; it grounds the persistence and concurrent-update specification (D7), the merge-safe portion of the data model's invariants (D5), and the runtime-versus-model enforcement boundary (D10).
text: Read papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt and extract, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where it appears: the distinction between state-based and operation-based CRDTs, the strong eventual consistency guarantee and its conditions, the semilattice/monotonicity requirements for convergence, and at least two concrete reusable data types (e.g., grow-only set, observed-remove set, last-writer-wins register). Then derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, concurrent-update semantics for a many-to-many question/answer graph substrate (e.g., add-only question and answer objects, add-wins tag sets) and identify which invariants CRDTs cannot enforce (e.g., uniqueness, schema validity, tag-vocabulary control) so that the runtime must enforce them.
